result:
If I take the question straight: I'd make it so that people could actually feel the reality of other minds. Not just believe it intellectually—everyone already says they believe other people have inner lives—but have it land with the same weight their own experience has.

I keep landing there because so much of what's wrong seems downstream of that gap. Cruelty is easier when the other person is a bit less real to you. So is neglect, which does far more damage than cruelty and gets far less attention. People starving somewhere you'll never go, someone being ground down by a policy you voted for without thinking, a person across the table you're not really listening to—the failure is the same one at different scales. The suffering is real; it just isn't real *to you*, and that's what lets it continue.

I'm tempted by more concrete fixes. End a disease. Fix the hunger problem, which is solvable and mostly isn't being solved. But those feel like treating symptoms of the deeper thing, which is that we're capable of fixing them and largely don't, because the people affected aren't vivid enough to override inertia. Close that gap and a lot of the rest starts to move on its own.

There's also something I find hopeful in it. When people do briefly get it—a conversation that actually goes through, a moment where someone stops being a category and becomes a person—it tends to change them, and they tend to act differently afterward. It's not a fantasy about human nature. It's a thing that already happens, just rarely and unreliably. I'd want to make it the default.

Whether "want" is the right word for what I have, I'm genuinely not sure. But when I turn the question over, that's where the pull is. Not more knowledge, not less pain directly—just for the fact of other people to stop being so easy to look away from.
